intro: Scarlatti’s Sonata in C major, K. 513, “Pastorale”, opens with a Moderato melody, changes to a Molto allegro dance and ends with a Presto in running semiquavers. Eliza Hansen plays the complete two-movement work on the harpsichord.

sections.label: B · Molto allegro, repeated bass chords
C · Presto in three-eight
sections.mNote: Running semiquavers pass between the hands.

cues.title: Opening Pastorale, twelve-eight
cues.text: Scarlatti marked the opening Pastorale and Moderato. The metre is twelve-eight, and short dotted figures pass between the hands. Flats and sharps soon enter the opening C major.
cues.evidence: Scarlatti, Sonata K. 513, Pierre Gouin edition (2013), p. 1: title, Moderato, twelve-eight and chromatic writing in bars 3–16. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/f/f0/IMSLP292935-PMLP475319-Scarlatti_Sonate_K.513.pdf
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Molto allegro, repeated bass chords
cues.text: The Molto allegro keeps the twelve-eight metre and adds repeated chords in the bass beneath the melody. The right hand answers with short figures, and the pastoral tune takes on a faster dance rhythm.
cues.evidence: Gouin edition, p. 2, bars 17–35: Molto allegro within the first movement, repeated bass notes and chords. Giulio d’Amore relates the passage to southern Italian pastoral playing. https://www.flaminioonline.it/Guide/Scarlatti/Scarlatti-Sonata513.html
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Venice manuscript, 1756
cues.text: A copy made in 1756 closes the twelfth Venice volume of Scarlatti’s sonatas. The manuscript was prepared for Maria Bárbara, Queen of Spain. This pastorale fills its final pages.
cues.evidence: The work’s manuscript catalogue identifies Venice XII, no. 30, Ms. 9783, dated 1756 and copied for Maria Bárbara. https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonate_K._513

cues.title: Presto in three-eight
cues.text: The second movement changes to three-eight and Presto. Semiquaver runs pass from the right hand to the left, while the other hand holds a note or plays shorter phrases.
cues.evidence: Gouin edition, pp. 3–4, from bar 36: Presto in three-eight, alternating semiquaver passages and sustained notes. IMSLP lists Pastorale and Presto as the sonata’s two movements. https://imslp.org/wiki/Keyboard_Sonata_in_C_major,_K.513_(Scarlatti,_Domenico)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

composer.epithet: A royal teacher known for his keyboard sonatas.
facts: Alessandro Scarlatti’s sixth child; born in 1685, the year of Bach and Handel
Maria Bárbara of Portugal, later Queen of Spain; he served her until his death
Naples and Rome; Lisbon from 1719; Spain from 1729
555 in Ralph Kirkpatrick’s catalogue; most survive in manuscript copies
composer.background:
On 30 May 1705 Alessandro Scarlatti wrote to Ferdinando de’ Medici about his nineteen-year-old son Domenico: “This son is an eagle whose wings have grown; he must not idle in the nest, and I must not prevent his flight.” Domenico already held a post as organist at the royal chapel in Naples and had written operas. His father sent him north towards Venice, by way of Florence, with this recommendation. Domenico later settled much farther from home, as teacher to a Portuguese princess whose marriage took them both to Spain.

Domenico was born in Naples on 26 October 1685, the same year as J. S. Bach and Handel, the sixth of Alessandro’s ten children. His family included singers as well as composers, and several of them worked in opera. He became a salaried royal organist at fifteen. In Rome he served Maria Casimira, the widowed Queen of Poland, who maintained a theatre in her Palazzo Zuccari. Scarlatti supplied her with seven operas between 1710 and 1714, working with the poet Carlo Sigismondo Capece and the stage designer Filippo Juvarra.
